chapter_name: What is a Good Book? by John Ruskin
learning_objective: 📚 Discover the true purpose of reading, and learn how to dig deep into a book like a miner digging for gold to find the author's true mind!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: अल्पकालिक (बहुत कम समय तक रहने वाला)
कुलीन वर्ग / श्रेष्ठ वर्ग (यहाँ अर्थ है ज्ञानियों का वर्ग)
चीर-फाड़ करना / गहराई से विश्लेषण करना

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Ruskin divides books into two classes: 'Books of the Hour' (useful for a short time, like newspapers, travelogues, or temporary guides) and 'Books of All Time' (true literature containing timeless wisdom and truth).

People desire to meet kings, queens, and famous elites. Ruskin argues that the true aristocracy is available on our bookshelves! We can converse with the greatest minds of human history (Shakespeare, Plato) anytime we want, simply by opening a book.

A good reader is like an Australian miner. You must use your mind as a pickaxe. The author's true meaning is the gold, hidden deep beneath the surface of the words. You must dig, sweat, and dissect the sentences to extract the real value.

Ruskin warns against reading just to confirm what we already believe. We should read to find out what the *author* thinks. We must submit our mind to the author's superior intellect to truly learn something new.

He insists that a truly educated person must look at words very carefully. You must know their exact meanings, their origins (etymology), and their nuances, because great authors use words with absolute, surgical precision.

fun_activity.title: ⛏️ Be a Word Miner
fun_activity.instructions: Take the word 'Alphabet'. Do you know where it comes from? It comes from combining the first two letters of the Greek language: 'Alpha' and 'Beta'. This is what Ruskin means by mining words for their deep origins!

exam_tips: 📌 The distinction between 'Books of the Hour' (ephemeral) and 'Books of All Time' (immutable) is the most critical concept. Be ready to give examples of both.
📌 Explain Ruskin's metaphor of the 'miner'. The rock is the book, the pickaxe is the reader's intellect, and the gold is the author's true meaning.
📌 Ruskin believes reading is hard work, not lazy entertainment. You must put in effort to understand great literature.
quick_recap: ⭐ Good books are the written voices of the wisest people who ever lived.
⭐ Ruskin criticizes people who spend heavily on wine and lavish dinners but refuse to spend money on good books.
⭐ The essay is actually an excerpt from his famous lecture collection, 'Sesame and Lilies'.
